stories.title: Time may be far stranger than we realize. Scientists have a way to test it
summary: Time may be far stranger than we realize, and scientists have proposed a way to detect clocks experiencing multiple flows of time simultaneously.
Using atomic clocks with dramatically enhanced sensitivity, researchers hope to reveal a never-before-observed quantum effect that could transform our understanding of time and gravity.

stories.title: A giant star swallowed another star. James Webb reveals the aftermath
summary: Astronomers have witnessed a spectacular cosmic collision in the Andromeda galaxy, where a small star spiraled into a giant star 18,000 times brighter than the Sun, triggering a violent eruption.
NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope captured the aftermath just 47 days later, revealing new details about how two stars can merge into one.

stories.title: Who was buried in Westminster Abbey's Roman coffin? A 150-year mystery may be solved
summary: A mysterious skeleton discovered in a Roman sarcophagus at Westminster Abbey may finally be identified after more than 150 years.
New dating evidence suggests the remains belonged to a high-ranking medieval abbot who was buried inside a centuries-old recycled Roman coffin.

stories.title: A 50-year-old theory about evolution may have been wrong all along
summary: A decades-old theory suggesting that evolution protects its most important genes from mutations has been dealt a major blow.
An extensive new analysis of mutations in bacteria and yeast found no evidence that essential genes mutate less frequently than other genes.
Researchers say earlier studies may have been misled by harmful mutations that disappeared through natural selection before scientists could detect them.

stories.title: Even scientists can't agree on what science actually is
summary: Scientists cannot agree on what science actually is, and a new study finds their views are surprisingly more divided than those of the general public.
The findings could help explain public frustration with scientific uncertainty and raise questions about how artificial intelligence might reshape future discoveries.

stories.title: Scientists say the human family tree may need a radical rewrite
summary: The human family tree may need a major overhaul.

New research from Monash University challenges the traditional classification of our ancient ancestors, arguing that species such as Australopithecus and Paranthropus should be grouped within our own genus, Homo.
As scientists uncover more fossils and analyze evolutionary relationships, the boundaries that once separated these ancient relatives are becoming increasingly difficult to defend.

stories.title: How red squirrels made island their home
summary: Conservationists say that, with red squirrels dwindling in the UK, Jersey is an "important refuge".

stories.title: After 8 years in space, a groundbreaking X-ray telescope finally opens its eyes
summary: After eight years and 10 billion kilometers in space, a groundbreaking X-ray telescope heading to Mercury has captured its first cosmic observations and is performing even better than scientists expected.
The instrument could soon reveal Mercury's hidden chemical secrets and transform our understanding of how the solar system's smallest planet formed.
